steps_tex: Find the value of both sides of each statement and compare.
$(a)$: $8 \times 9 = 72$ and $70 + 2 = 72$. The same value, so True.

$(c)$: $48 \div 3 = 16$ and $4 \times 4 = 16$. The same value, so True.
$(d)$: $89 - 9 = 80$ and $90 + 0 = 90$. Different values, so False.
$(e)$: $25 + 10 = 35$ and $45 - 10 = 35$. The same value, so True.

item.question: Complete the following statements such that they are true. (a): 7 × 6 = ___ + 17; (b): 87 + 6 = ___ × 31; (c): 63 + ___ = 74 − 4; (d): ___ ÷ 9 = 16 ÷ 2.
steps_tex: Find the side that has no blank, then make the other side the same.
$(a)$: the left side $7 \times 6$ is $42$, so the blank is $42 - 17 = 25$. Check: $25 + 17 = 42$.
$(b)$: the left side $87 + 6$ is $93$, so the blank is $93 \div 31 = 3$. Check: $3 \times 31 = 93$.
$(c)$: the right side $74 - 4$ is $70$, so the blank is $70 - 63 = 7$. Check: $63 + 7 = 70$.
$(d)$: the right side $16 \div 2$ is $8$, so the blank is $8 \times 9 = 72$. Check: $72 \div 9 = 8$.

item.question: Think about the following statements and find examples as suggested below. (a): “When two odd numbers are added, the sum is even.” Find 5 examples for the above statement. Can you find an example to show that the statement can be false?
steps_tex: The statement: when two odd numbers are added, the sum is even.
Five examples: $1 + 3 = 4$, $3 + 5 = 8$, $7 + 9 = 16$, $5 + 11 = 16$ and $9 + 9 = 18$. All the sums are even.
Try more: $11 + 13 = 24$ and $15 + 1 = 16$. These sums are even too.
Why: each odd number has one left over when counted in pairs, and the two left overs make one more pair, so the sum has none left over.
No example shows the statement false, so it is always true.

Three examples that work: half of $8$ is $4$, half of $12$ is $6$ and half of $20$ is $10$. All are even.
Three examples that do not work: half of $6$ is $3$, half of $10$ is $5$ and half of $14$ is $7$. These are odd.
Some work and some fail, so the statement is not always true. It is sometimes true.
